Seminar Title:

Human Gait Recognition in Different Covariate Conditions using Deep Learning Techniques

Seminar Type:

Mohammad Iman Junaid ( Rollno : 520ec6013)

Samit Ari

Abstract:

Gait Recognition uses visual surveillance to identify people based on the style of their walk. Despite the recent advances in the field of deep learning, the performance of gait recognition is still hard to achieve when it is encountered with covariate conditions, including view angle, clothing, carrying condition, walking speed, and environment. Traditional CNNs lack the ability to learn long-range spatial&ndashtemporal dependencies, global context, and fine-grained spatial information. Considering the drawbacks, this research proposes a series of deep learning-based gait recognition systems that improve the spatial, temporal, and multi-level features representation. First, a multi-scale sequential learning attention-based CNN (MASL-Net) is built to extract multi-scale spatial features, pay attention to discriminative regions, and model the temporal dependency with a bidirectional gated recurrent unit (Bi-GRU). Then, a joint spatial&ndashtemporal (ST) modulation network composed of attention-based CNNs, bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM), and temporal attention is proposed to model spatial&ndashtemporal correlations. Next, a residual dense back-flow attention network (RDBA-Net) is added to further promote the propagation of features by integrating dual-branch hybrid self-attention and residual dense blocks and back-flow semantic information. In addition, a pyramidal feature aggregation network (PFA-Net) is designed based on densely connected residual feature enhancement blocks and pyramidal multi-level feature fusion which can extract fine-grained spatial and semantic information. Finally, a two-branch silhouette&ndashpose fusion network (SiPoF-Net) is proposed by combining the silhouette-based and pose-based representations via the attention-enhanced CNN and spatial&ndashtemporal graph convolutional learning, and the score-based fusion for robust silhouette recognition. Four public gait datasets are used to comprehensively test the proposed frameworks in various covariate and occlusion scenarios. The results in both quantitative and qualitative aspects show that the proposed methods consistently outperform the existing state-of-the-art methods, thus proving their usefulness in gait recognition with robust and accurate results.
